description.p: CoreX is a lightweight hardware monitor for Linux that keeps you informed about your system's health at all times.

ul.li: Every sensor of your PC in one list: CPU and GPU temperatures, fan speeds, voltages, power, clocks, disks and network, each with its minimum and maximum
A dashboard with live charts per device, a hybrid view with the full list next to the charts, or charts only for the values you pick
An overview you put together yourself: choose its charts and their order
An always-on-top widget with the values you choose, visible while gaming, working or browsing
A widget editor: place every value where you want it, align them or arrange them in columns, add icons, pick text sizes, the widget size, the background opacity and a background picture
History of every sensor for up to a year, with charts and CSV export
Alerts above or below any value, with a desktop notification
A system report of your hardware and readings, ready to paste in a forum post
Dark, light or system theme
Rename sensors, hide the ones you do not need; CoreX remembers your layout
Can start with your system, straight into the widget
Light on resources: it reads the kernel directly, no background services
